batch

Class MediaBatchProcessor

  • java.lang.Object
    • batch.MediaBatchProcessor

  • public final class MediaBatchProcessor
extends java.lang.Object
    Automates the batch processing of media files by copying, renaming, and chronologically sorting them according to metadata timestamps. This is the engine core of the batch processing functionality.

    This processor implements a "surgical" strategy. It never modifies source files. Instead, it creates a renamed copy in the target directory and applies binary patches to the metadata segments of the copy to ensure chronological integrity across JPEG, TIFF, DNG, PNG, WebP, and HEIF formats.

    A built-in 10-second offset is applied to user-defined dates to prevent metadata collisions and ensure stable sorting in downstream applications, such as Windows Photos or Apple Photos.

    Since:
    5 May 2026
    Version:
    1.2
    Author:
    Trevor Maggs

      • execute

        public BatchMetrics execute()
                     throws BatchErrorException
        Begins the batch-processing workflow by preparing the target directory, initialising logging, and processing the configured media files.

        Note: Call addProgressListener(progressbar.ProgressListener) prior to calling this method if you wish to monitor execution progress via a progress bar or a type of console update indicator.

        Returns:
        the BatchMetrics summarising files scanned, files processed, and total bytes (cumulative)
        Throws:
        BatchErrorException - if an I/O error occurs during directory preparation or file processing

      • processRecord

        private long processRecord(MediaRecord record,
                           java.nio.file.attribute.FileTime effectiveTime,
                           java.lang.String newName)
                    throws BatchErrorException
        Handles the end-to-end processing of a single media record.

        The process follows a strict "copy-then-patch" sequence:

        1. Copy the source file to the target location.
        2. Apply binary metadata patches to the copied file using the calculated timestamp, if required.
        3. Update file-system timestamps.
        Parameters:
        record - the media file record to process
        effectiveTime - the calculated effective timestamp
        newName - the target filename to use for output
        Returns:
        the file size of the newly generated file, or -1 if processing was cancelled before completion
        Throws:
        BatchErrorException - if file I/O or metadata patching fails

      • calculateEffectiveTime

        private java.nio.file.attribute.FileTime calculateEffectiveTime(MediaRecord record,
                                                                int index)
        Determines the effective timestamp for a media record.

        If date changes are forced, the batch configuration guarantees that a user-defined date is available. A fixed 10-second offset is then applied based on the record position to ensure unique chronological ordering.

        Otherwise, the media record's natural timestamp is returned. The natural timestamp is determined by the metadata date when available, if no metadata date exists, the user-defined date is used when configured, otherwise the file's last modified time is used.

        Parameters:
        record - the media record being processed
        index - the current index used to calculate the 10-second offset
        Returns:
        the effective FileTime used for metadata and file-system updates

      • prepareTargetDirectory

        private void prepareTargetDirectory()
                             throws BatchErrorException
        Prepares the target directory by ensuring it exists and is empty.

        An exception is thrown if the target directory is identical to the source directory to prevent accidental data loss during cleanup.

        Throws:
        BatchErrorException - if source/target are identical or directory creation fails
